title: Maximum Sum of Two Non-Overlapping Subarrays
statement: Choose two blocks of consecutive elements from the integer array `nums`: one block of exactly `firstLen` elements and another of exactly `secondLen` elements. The two blocks may not share any index, but either one may come first in the array. Return the largest possible total of all elements inside the two blocks.
signature: int maxSumTwoNoOverlap(int[] nums, int firstLen, int secondLen)
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every pair of block positions costs O(n²) pairs, each needing a sum. Prefix sums make any block sum O(1), and a sweep removes the pair loop: fix where the **right** block ends, and the best left block is simply the best block that ends early enough, which only grows as the sweep moves right. Because either block may be on the left, track the best left block of each length.

## Approach

1. Build `prefix` so that `prefix[i]` is the sum of the first `i` numbers; a block ending before index `end` with length `len` sums to `prefix[end] - prefix[end - len]`.
2. Sweep `end` (the exclusive end of the right block) from `firstLen + secondLen` to `n`.
3. If the right block has length `secondLen`, the left `firstLen` block must end by `end - secondLen`; add that newly allowed block (`firstBefore`) into `bestFirst`. Symmetrically update `bestSecond` with `secondBefore`.
4. Try both layouts: `bestFirst + secondLast` and `bestSecond + firstLast`, and keep the largest in `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [0,6,5,2,2,5,1,9,4]`, `firstLen = 1`, `secondLen = 2`, so `prefix = [0,0,6,11,13,15,20,21,30,34]`.

- `end = 3`: `bestFirst = 0` (block `[0]`), `bestSecond = 6` (`[0,6]`); candidates `0 + 11` and `6 + 5`, so `best = 11`.
- `end = 4`: `bestFirst = 6`, `bestSecond = 11` (`[6,5]`); candidates `6 + 7` and `11 + 2`, so `best = 13`.
- `end = 6`: candidates `6 + 7` and `11 + 5`, so `best = 16`.
- `end = 8`: `secondLast = 10` (`[1,9]`) and `firstLast = 9` (`[9]`); candidates `6 + 10` and `11 + 9`, so `best = 20`.
- `end = 9`: candidates `6 + 13` and `11 + 4`; `best` stays `20`, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass for the prefix sums and one sweep.
- Space: O(n) for `prefix`.

## Pitfalls

- Handle both orders; checking only "first block on the left" misses answers like Example 1.
- The newly allowed left block must end exactly where the right block starts, so its end is `end - secondLen` (or `end - firstLen`), not `end`.
- Start the sweep at `firstLen + secondLen`, the first place where both blocks fit.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prefix` | prefix sums: `prefix[i]` is the sum of `nums[0..i-1]` |
| `end` | exclusive end of the right-hand block |
| `firstBefore`, `secondBefore` | the newest left block of each length that fits |
| `bestFirst`, `bestSecond` | best left block of each length seen so far |
| `firstLast`, `secondLast` | the right-hand block of each length ending at `end` |
| `best` | the largest total of two blocks found |
